head: e3e41bae376a29b27a9da7c111dfa841e8d43837
title: Reuse positive-document membership during reciprocal rank fusion evaluation
body:
## Change

Construct one positive-document set per query while evaluating dense, sparse and fused retrieval rankings. Each ranking currently scans the positive list once per retrieved document; large relevance sets make this membership work dominate evaluation.

The original positive list remains the source for normalization and prediction export, including its order and duplicate entries. The lookup set is rebuilt during each evaluation, so edits to samples between calls are reflected immediately. Ranking and tie behavior are unchanged.

## Validation and benchmark

[Exact-base CPU validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43916628776) compares base `9ac7fdb4` and candidate `e3e41bae` on PyTorch **2.6.0** and **2.14.1**. The **5 new compatibility cases pass on base and candidate**; with adjacent tests, the candidate passes **23 tests** in each environment. Cases include one/multiple/no positives, duplicate positive IDs, exact export ordering and repeated evaluation after sample mutation. All repository pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

The [benchmark](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/blob/83e1c683da360ab8d6028721fca1f4eeeaad6656/.validation/st-rrf-benchmark.py) measures the full evaluator with deterministic cached retrieval results, metric computation and prediction JSON export, using 20 queries, one warmup and five timed runs. All nine metrics and exported prediction digests match exactly.

| PyTorch 2.14.1 workload | Before median | After median | Ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 512 documents per retriever, 20 positives | 56.33 ms | 49.28 ms | 1.14× |
| 2,048 documents per retriever, 512 positives | 816.53 ms | 132.62 ms | 6.16× |

PyTorch 2.6.0 measured 1.21× and 5.93× for the same cases. These timings isolate evaluator overhead after retrieval; encoder inference is outside the benchmark.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped with investigation, implementation, compatibility tests and benchmarking.
